## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two things should be fixed: slugify mangles letters with accents and other non-ASCII letters, which breaks the description's promise to keep alphanumeric characters, and the PR description is missing the `## Testing` section that AGENTS.md requires.

## Changes
Adds `app/slug.py` with a `slugify` function that builds URL slugs from page titles. It also adds `tests/test_slug.py`, a parametrized test that checks ASCII titles, titles made only of hyphens, and empty titles.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters in slugs — The title "Crème Brûlée" becomes "cr-me-br-l-e", and "日本語" becomes "". This happens because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator, but the PR body says only "runs of non-alphanumeric characters" are replaced. — Pages with accented or non-Latin titles get broken URLs, and titles written entirely in non-Latin scripts all produce the same empty slug. — Fix: Either transliterate first with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop the combining marks, or match `[\W_]+` so Unicode letters are kept; then add those titles as cases in `test_slugify`.
- PR body — correctness — Add the required `## Testing` section — The PR description has no `## Testing` section, which breaks the rule at AGENTS.md:4: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Readers of the PR have no record of how the change was verified, as the project rules require.
